Let $u=\operatorname{tan}x$ and $v={x}^{2}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & ={sec}^{2}x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}\cdot {sec}^{2}x-\operatorname{tan}x\cdot 2x}{{({x}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{x(x{sec}^{2}x-2\operatorname{tan}x)}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{1}{{x}^{3}}\cdot (\,x{sec}^{2}x-2\operatorname{tan}x\,).\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u=-x$ and $v=9-2x.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =-1\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(9-2x)\cdot (-1)-(-x)\cdot (-2)}{{(9-2x)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{-9+2x-2x}{{(9-2x)}^{2}} \\  & =-\frac{9}{{(9-2x)}^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $u={log}_{3}⁡x=\frac{ln⁡x}{ln⁡3}$ and $v={x}^{2}.$ Then

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{xln⁡3}\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2x.\end{aligned}
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{({x}^{2}\cdot \frac{1}{xln⁡3}-\frac{ln⁡x}{ln⁡3}\cdot 2x)}{({x}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{x}{ln⁡3}-\frac{2xln⁡x}{ln⁡3})}{{x}^{4}} \\  & =\frac{x-2xln⁡x}{{x}^{4}ln⁡3} \\  & =\frac{x(1-2ln⁡x)}{{x}^{4}ln⁡3} \\  & =\frac{1-2ln⁡x}{{x}^{3}ln⁡3} \\  & =(\,1-2ln⁡x\,)\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{3}ln⁡3}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-cos⁡x\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=cos⁡x.
$$

Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}-u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{sin⁡x\cdot (-cos⁡x)-(1-sin⁡x)\cdot cos⁡x}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{cos⁡x(-sin⁡x-1+sin⁡x)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =\frac{cos⁡x\cdot (-1)}{{sin}^{2}⁡x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{sin⁡x}\cdot \frac{cos⁡x}{sin⁡x} \\  & =-csc⁡xcot⁡x.\end{aligned}
$$
